row.text: In thispaper, we present an approach for enhancing the accuracy of LLMs by integrating them withData Commons, a vast, open-source repository of public statistics from trusted organizationslike the United Nations (UN), Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and globalcensus bureaus.

props.name: Data Commons
props.description: Open-source repository of public statistics from trusted organizations, used as the external data source the LLM queries.
props.grounding_span: In thispaper, we present an approach for enhancing the accuracy of LLMs by integrating them withData Commons, a vast, open-source repository of public statistics from trusted organizationslike the United Nations (UN), Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and globalcensus bureaus.

row.text: We explore two primary methods: Retrieval Interleaved Generation (RIG),where the LLM is trained to produce natural language queries to retrieve data from DataCommons, and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), where relevant data tables are fetchedfrom Data Commons and used to augment the LLM's prompt.

props.name: Retrieval Interleaved Generation
props.description: Method in which the LLM is trained to produce natural language queries that retrieve statistics from a data store.
props.grounding_span: We explore two primary methods: Retrieval Interleaved Generation (RIG),where the LLM is trained to produce natural language queries to retrieve data from DataCommons, and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), where relevant data tables are fetchedfrom Data Commons and used to augment the LLM's prompt.

row.text: In RAG, an auxiliary retrievalsystem is used to identify background knowledge from a large corpora that is relevant to auser’s query.

row.text: |  [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization "Organization") or [Person](https://schema.org/Person "Person") | A maintainer of a [Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset), software package ([SoftwareApplication](https://schema.org/SoftwareApplication)), or other [Project](https://schema.org/Project). A maintainer is a [Person](https://schema.org/Person) or [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [maintainer](https://schema.org/maintainer) is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset), it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [isBasedOn](https://schema.org/isBasedOn) property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.

row.text: In this article, to help further the Comunikos project agenda and more generally encourage work measuring and communicating data uncertainty, we provide a methodological review and categorisation of uncertainty measures and their sources for economic statistics.

props.name: data uncertainty
props.description: Uncertainty in data that the article reviews, categorises and seeks to measure and communicate.
props.grounding_span:
In this article, to help further the Comunikos project agenda and more generally encourage
work measuring and communicating data uncertainty, we provide a methodological review
and categorisation of uncertainty measures and their sources for economic statistics.

row.text: The total survey error of an estimate is considered as an indicator of data quality.

A maintainer is a [Person](https://schema.org/Person) or [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [maintainer](https://schema.org/maintainer) is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset), it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [isBasedOn](https://schema.org/isBasedOn) property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.

row.text: Morgenstern (1950), as drawn on throughout this review, distinguishes ten sources of uncertainty: (1) lack of designed experiments; (2) hiding of information, lies; (3) the training of observers; (4) errors from questionnaires; (5) mass observations; (6) lack of deﬁnition and classiﬁcation; (7) errors of instruments; (8) the factor of time; (9) observations of unique phenomena; (10) interdependence and stability of errors.

row.text: |  [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization "Organization") or [Person](https://schema.org/Person "Person") | A maintainer of a [Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset), software package ([SoftwareApplication](https://schema.org/SoftwareApplication)), or other [Project](https://schema.org/Project). A maintainer is a [Person](https://schema.org/Person) or [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [maintainer](https://schema.org/maintainer) is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset), it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [isBasedOn](https://schema.org/isBasedOn) property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.

row.text: |  [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization "Organization") or [Person](https://schema.org/Person "Person") | A maintainer of a [Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset), software package ([SoftwareApplication](https://schema.org/SoftwareApplication)), or other [Project](https://schema.org/Project). A maintainer is a [Person](https://schema.org/Person) or [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [maintainer](https://schema.org/maintainer) is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset), it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [isBasedOn](https://schema.org/isBasedOn) property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.
